key_insight: SpatialClaw argues that an agent’s spatial reasoning performance is not limited only by the model or tools themselves, but by the action interface used to call those tools. A better interface can make vision-language agents more effective at open-ended 3D spatial tasks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of weak spatial reasoning in vision-language models, especially when they rely on external perception tools. It studies why existing tool-invocation interfaces can bottleneck an agent’s ability to reason about object location, relationships, and motion in 3D.
method: Analyzes how different action interfaces affect agent performance in spatial reasoning tasks.
Introduces SpatialClaw, a redesigned interface for invoking specialist perception modules more effectively.
Evaluates the agent’s ability to perform open-ended spatial reasoning under the new interface design.
impact: For AI practitioners, this work highlights that interface design is a key lever for improving agentic reasoning, not just model scale or tool quality. It suggests that better action schemas can unlock stronger performance in real-world multimodal systems.

paper_title: SpatialClaw: Rethinking Action Interface for Agentic Spatial Reasoning
paper_authors: Seokju Cho, Ryo Hachiuma, Abhishek Badki, Hang Su, Byung-Kwan Lee
